questions.q: What does the Oracle Universal Installer (OUI) actually do, per this lesson?
options: Installs the Oracle Database software into an Oracle Home — it does not create a database
Only manages user accounts and privileges
Creates a fully configured database with sample data
Configures the Oracle Net Listener exclusively
questions.explain: OUI installs the software (binaries, libraries, utilities) into an Oracle Home; no database exists yet at the end of an OUI run.

questions.q: What is the role of the Database Configuration Assistant (DBCA)?
options: It installs the Oracle Database software itself
It is the tool that actually creates a database, run after the software is already installed
It replaces the need for an Oracle Home entirely
It is only used for backup and recovery operations
questions.explain: DBCA is run after OUI and is where you actually create a database — a CDB with one or more PDBs, in the default multitenant approach.

questions.q: Why does Oracle separate 'install the software' from 'create the database' into two different tools, per this lesson?
options: It's an arbitrary historical accident with no practical benefit
Because the same Oracle Home can be used to create and run more than one database, and software upgrades are a different operation from touching any database's data
Because DBCA cannot run without a GUI
Because Oracle does not support creating more than one database per server
questions.explain: The lesson explains this separation is deliberate: one Oracle Home can host multiple databases, and software maintenance is decoupled from any individual database.

questions.q: What can both OUI and DBCA do to support installs at scale, per this lesson?
options: Skip the prerequisite checks entirely
Automatically install on every server on a network simultaneously
Run non-interactively from a response file, for scripted/repeatable installs
Only run once per Oracle Home, ever
questions.explain: Both tools support silent, response-file-driven runs, which is how most organizations install Oracle reliably across many servers.

questions.q: What is the last step in the ordered high-level flow this lesson describes, from a bare machine to a running database?
options: Verifying the database by connecting with SQL*Plus
Meeting the OS-level prerequisites
Running the Oracle Universal Installer
Running DBCA to create the database
questions.explain: The flow ends with connecting via SQL*Plus to confirm the instance is up and the database is open.
